questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: As a Spanish student it's always relevant to go to a Spanish speaking country and the University of Buenos Aires is the best in Latin America and has a good academic offer, especially within social sciences. Besides that, Buenos Aires is a very vibrant city with a rich cultural life.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: The international relations office sent out a lot of useful information about the introductory meeting and the enrollment process the last month before arrival. However, it was very difficult to find the necessary information about the academic offer and the credit system before the deadline for applying for "forhåndsgodkendelse" at UCPH. The person in charge at the University of Buenos Aires took a long time to reply to emails.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: We had an introductory meeting where they explained the enrollment process, the course offer and practical information about the grading scale, how to use the virtual campus and the study life in general.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: As I started looking for accommodation well in advance, it was quite easy. In general, it is easier to find housing in Buenos Aires than in many European cities where prices can be high and the offer can be limited. I mostly looked at Airbnb, since it is safer and more reliable.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: In general, it is easier to find housing in Buenos Aires than in many European cities where prices can be high and the offer can be limited. Though, I would recommend looking for housing in safe and clean areas such as Palermo, Recoleta and the northern part of the city. Even though Buenos Aires is generally safer than many other Latin American cities, the city center and the southern part of the city can be slightly unsafe by night.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: We had to go to the international relations office a certain day at a certain time and tell the secretary which courses we wanted. Then she signed us up.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The secretary of international relations at the faculty was always available.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Since I had checked the schedules before registering to avoid overlaps, I got all the courses I wanted and had a "forhåndsgodkendelse" for.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: When looking for courses before applying for "forhåndsgodkendelse", it is a good idea to look at last year's course offer and schedules. The mandatory courses and most of the elective courses are repeated every year.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level of all my courses was quite high, especially the one I had at the master in Political Sciences.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: All my courses were taught in smaller groups (up to 30 students) which made it possible to have a good dialogue with professors and fellow students, such as those at UCPH. On the other hand, two of my subjects were workshops, so there were more hands-on assignments and less reading.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Taller de Redacción y Géneros Periodísticos, Taller Radial and Regímenes Políticos en América Latina.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend all my courses because I had very inspiring professors and learned a lot about Argentina and Latin America in general.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Since the Argentinian economy is rather unstable, prices are unpredictable and it is difficult to make a budget prior to arrival. During the time I was there, the prices rose every month. The public transportation prices doubled. The best thing you can do is a "worst case scenario" budget and expect prices similar to those in Europe.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: The supermarkets were as expensive as in Denmark, which I didn't expect. Services such as Uber and the hairdresser were quite cheap.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I know there were a lot of activities but I didn't participate in any of them, since I did a lot of activities outside of the university.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Buenos Aires is a very vibrant city with many cultural activities such as art and music events, pop-up markets, film-screenings, sport activities and the like. There are several Instagram profiles that make "what to do in Buenos Aires this weekend" posts with overviews of everything that's happening. I would highly recommend participating in those activities since it's a good way to get to know the city and meet people outside of campus.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: There are plenty of nice places to visit just outside of Buenos Aires such as Tigre and Colonia in Uruguay. Besides that, Argentina is a huge country with many nice places to visit. During my stay, I went to Salta and Jujuy, Bariloche and Iguazú. The only thing to keep in mind is that, due to the long distances, it is almost always necessary to travel by plane. Though, domestic flight tickets are often cheap and you can buy them one or two days in advance.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I found it quite easy since I already lived in Costa Rica, Mexico and Spain before doing my exchange semester in Buenos Aires. People are very kind and helpful and since the Argentinians are very proud of their country, they want you to get the best impression of it. Also, Buenos Aires is more European than other Latin American cities when it comes to culture, food and architecture.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: In my case, it happened automatically because I had many group assignments. The local students are very open and easy to talk to. They would often offer me mate (a typical Argentinian drink) which is a sign that they consider you a part of the group. The best you can do is being open-minded and showing interest in their culture.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: In general the Argentinians are less punctual and more spontaneous which sometimes makes it difficult to plan things. Also, they are very proud, so it is best to avoid criticizing their culture, even though you mean it in a good way.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The kindness of the people. They don't care if you are a foreigner and you are only there for six months, they do everything they can to make you feel part of the community.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
To find out well in advance what information/documents you need to apply for "forhåndsgodkendelse", complete the enrollment and apply for a visa. The University of Buenos Aires and UCPH have different processes and deadlines, and your contact persons at each university are not necessarily aware of that.

Making local friends. It is a good way to get to know the culture, discover places in the city you wouldn't have found on your own and practice your Spanish. 

If possible, to travel around Argentina. It is a beautiful country with huge regional differences and a lot to offer.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Each professor organises teaching and learning activities differently. Some don't use the virtual campus, and you have to get in touch with them by mail. Some choose to do online classes instead of in-person classes. They also have different assessment methods. Therefore, you can't always ask your fellow exchange students or the international relations office for advice. If you have questions about the specific course, it is often better to ask the professor directly.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: All the amazing people I met. They really made Buenos Aires feel like home.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: I didn't meet significant challenges besides the continuously changing prices.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
